# Snippets

Rendered with `{% render 'name', param: value %}`. Parameters come from each snippet's LiquidDoc header.

## ai-label

File: `snippets/ai-label.liquid`

A small "AI" label for the bottom right corner of an image, shown when the
image's own alt text says it is AI made: the lowercased alt contains
"ai generated" or "ai altered" (a hyphen counts as a space, so "AI-generated"
matches too). Merchants control it by writing that in the image's alt text in
Shopify; there is nothing else to configure.

Renders nothing otherwise. The label is decorative (aria-hidden): the alt text
already tells screen reader users the same thing. It is not translated: "AI"
is the same in every language the theme ships.

The parent must be position: relative (the gallery frame, .media and .hero__media
are; product cards are positioned by the .product-card rule in base.css). Colors are
fixed black and white, not tokens, because the label sits on a photo and must read
on it in both color schemes. Styles are in base.css because several pages use it.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alt` | `string` | yes | The image's alt text |

```liquid
{% render 'ai-label', alt: media.alt %}
```

## badge-pick

File: `snippets/badge-pick.liquid`

Picks the badges a product shows: prints one `handle~tag` item per badge, space separated (the badge's handle, and the
product's own tag that names it, handleized, for a link to the tag's collection), the
lowest priority number first (ties keep the tag order), and nothing when no tag matches. A tag `badge-<handle>` names
the metaobject entry (type badge) with that handle; a tag whose handle has no entry, or whose entry has no label or
color, is skipped. The tag `new` and the tag `badge-new` both name the badge `new`, which works with no entry at all
(a built-in "New", see the `badge` snippet); an entry with the handle `new` replaces its label and color. An entry that
shows only on the card or only on the product page is skipped in the other context. The same handle is listed once,
with the first tag that names it, except that the plain tag `new` wins over `badge-new` when a product has both (the owner's
rule: the merchant keeps the catalog consistent).
**Sale is a computed badge, and opt-in**: a product whose compare-at price is above its price counts as named by `sale`, with no tag,
but only when a badge entry with the handle `sale` exists (and has a label and a color). There is no built-in Sale. The entry's
label, color, `show_on` and priority apply like any other. It prints `sale~` with no tag, so the caller makes no link of it.
At most four badge tags are read, and at most two badges are printed (the two with the lowest priority numbers: a card shows the first, the product page both). A leaf snippet on purpose: it renders nothing, so no render is nested deeper than
the card's own image (AGENTS.md rule 7). Decision record: docs/decisions/045-badges-are-a-metaobject-mapped-from-tags.md.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product` | `product` | yes | The product whose tags name the badges |
| `context` | `string` | yes | Where the badge will show: 'card' or 'product' |

```liquid
{%- capture picks -%}{%- render 'badge-pick', product: product, context: 'card' -%}{%- endcapture -%}
```

## badge

File: `snippets/badge.liquid`

One badge by handle: the label of the badge metaobject entry with that handle, on the entry's color, with the text
color chosen for contrast (white or black, whichever has the higher contrast ratio), so a merchant's color can never
produce unreadable text. The handle `new` with no usable entry (missing, or without a label or color) is the built-in
"New" (`products.new`, blue from --color-new). Any other handle without an entry prints nothing (there is no built-in Sale: it exists only as an entry). The label is text, not
an image. The look is the shared `.badge` recipe in assets/base.css; the caller adds the classes for where it sits and
for the colors (`background: var(--badge-bg); color: var(--badge-fg)`). Decision record:
docs/decisions/045-badges-are-a-metaobject-mapped-from-tags.md.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `string` | yes | The badge handle, as printed by the `badge-pick` snippet |
| `class` | `string` | no | Extra classes, for example the card's position class |
| `url` | `string` | no | Makes the badge a link to this URL, with rel="nofollow" (a tag's collection page is a filtered duplicate, not a page to rank). Without it the badge is a plain span. |

```liquid
{%- render 'badge', handle: badge_pick, class: 'product-card__badge product-card__badge--custom' -%}
```

## breadcrumbs

File: `snippets/breadcrumbs.liquid`

Breadcrumb trail and its BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, built once from the same
data so they can never disagree. This is the ONLY place a BreadcrumbList is
emitted; do not add another.

Rules (Google and WCAG):
- The trail reflects a stable site hierarchy, not the visitor's click path.
- Product: product metafield singi.primary_collection, else the collection the
  visitor came from, else the product's first collection in Shopify's order (never
  "all" or "frontpage"), else just Home > Product. So a direct visit to a product
  still shows where it lives.
- Collection and product ancestors come from the collection metafield
  singi.parent_collection, up to three levels, and, when a collection has none,
  from where the collection sits in the breadcrumb menu (theme setting
  Navigation > Breadcrumb menu, default main-menu). Metafields win over the menu.
  Pages, blogs and the collections list use the menu the same way (they have no
  metafield); an article uses its blog's place in the menu, then the blog, then itself.
  Define both metafields with `npm run seo:metafields`.
- Absolute URLs in JSON-LD; the last JSON-LD item is the current page, which is not a link and
  is not drawn in the visible trail (the heading already says it).
- The visible trail is drawn only when there is at least one ancestor besides the
  current page. A lone current page adds nothing the heading does not, so the
  nav is omitted (the JSON-LD still lists Home and the page). Sections then get
  their normal top padding, because the breadcrumb spacing rule needs the nav.
- Home is in the JSON-LD but not in the visible trail (saves space).
- Semantic nav > ol > li, separators drawn by CSS.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `string` | yes | product, collection, collections, article, blog or page |

```liquid
{% render 'breadcrumbs', kind: 'product' %}
```

## consent-dialog

File: `snippets/consent-dialog.liquid`

The cookie dialog: one native, modal <dialog> over a scrim (a decision is needed before the page is used), shown by assets/consent.js only to a visitor
Shopify's region rules say must be asked and who has not answered yet (`shouldShowBanner()` and `currentVisitorConsent()`
of the Customer Privacy API). The answer is recorded with `setTrackingConsent()`, only after a click, never automatically.
Accept all and Reject all are the same size and weight (both primary buttons; Save choices replaces them once Preferences is open); Preferences opens Essential (always on), Analytics, Marketing and
Preferences. A footer button (`data-consent-open`, sections/footer.liquid) reopens it with the current choices.
On a store with more than one country or language the first ask also shows the visitor's country and language (the market
Shopify resolved, with the currency) and lets them change either, so one click on Accept all or Reject all confirms the
consent and the region together; the footer's Cookie settings button reopens the consent part only, and the footer
selector stays the way to change region later. Nothing redirects: the country and language are preselected from what Shopify's
suggestion endpoint detects for the visitor (assets/consent.js), and apply only when the visitor answers. The words are Shopify's own
cookie banner copy, translated and edited in the admin, fetched from the Storefront API on a real store host; the `consent` strings
here are the fallback (and what the dev server shows, where that call cannot be made).
Needs JavaScript: without it nothing non-essential runs and the dialog never shows. Rendered first in the body when the
theme setting "Show the theme's cookie dialog" is on (and Shopify's own banner is off). Decision record:
docs/decisions/046-the-cookie-dialog-is-the-themes-and-shopifys-api-records-the-answer.md.

```liquid
{% render 'consent-dialog' %}
```

## image

File: `snippets/image.liquid`

Responsive image with the loading strategy decided in one place.

- priority: the LCP candidate. Eager, fetchpriority=high and a preload hint.
  Use for at most one image per page.
- eager: visible in the first viewport but not the LCP candidate. Eager only.
- neither: lazy and async decoded.

Width and height attributes come from image_tag, so layout never shifts.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | `image` | yes | The image to render |
| `sizes` | `string` | no | The sizes attribute. Default: 100vw |
| `widths` | `string` | no | Comma separated srcset widths |
| `width` | `number` | no | Largest width to request. Default: 1600 |
| `alt` | `string` | no | Alt text. Default: the image's own alt text |
| `decorative` | `boolean` | no | Empty alt text, for a thumbnail whose product name is right next to it |
| `class` | `string` | no | Class for the img element |
| `priority` | `boolean` | no | Mark as the LCP image |
| `eager` | `boolean` | no | Load eagerly without a preload |
| `crossorigin` | `string` | no | Set to anonymous when scripts must read the pixels (assets/image-tone.js) |

```liquid
{% render 'image', image: section.settings.image, priority: true, sizes: '100vw' %}
{% render 'image', image: product.featured_image, sizes: '(min-width: 56em) 25vw, 50vw' %}
```

## localization-selector

File: `snippets/localization-selector.liquid`

Country and language selector, rendered in the footer. Hidden unless the store
has more than one country or language.

Plain markup: one `localization` form whose options are submit buttons, so it
works with no JavaScript. Choosing an option posts to Shopify, which sets the
market and returns to the current page.

Performance: `localization.available_countries` can hold about 240 countries
on a store with a "Rest of world" market. With more than 12 countries the list
is not rendered on page load. It is fetched the first time the selector is
opened, through the Section Rendering API (assets/localization.js). That is
detected with `section.index`, which is nil in Section Rendering API responses
and in the theme editor, so those always get the full list.

Must be rendered inside a section (it reads `section.id` and `section.index`).

```liquid
{% render 'localization-selector' %}
```

## newsletter

File: `snippets/newsletter.liquid`

Newsletter signup: a Shopify customer form (no JavaScript) that tags the new subscriber
"newsletter". The email input and the Subscribe button are one joined control: they share one
border, radius and height, and the button's side follows the reading direction (RTL safe).

Used by the footer and by blocks/newsletter.liquid. Each use needs its own `id`, so the label
and input stay paired when the form appears twice on a page.

Consent. Submitting the form is what subscribes the visitor: Shopify records the signup as accepting marketing.
The theme ships no legal wording. A merchant writes the theme setting "Consent note" (what the subscriber
agrees to, with a link to the privacy policy), shown under the form and tied to the email input as its
description. With the setting "Ask visitors to tick a box" the note becomes the label of an unticked checkbox
that is required before the form can be sent; the checkbox is a gate in the page, not a second field sent to
Shopify. Double opt-in is a Shopify admin setting; the setting "Confirmation message" lets the form say so.
Not legal advice. Decision record: docs/decisions/029-newsletter-consent-is-merchant-written-and-ships-no-legal-copy.md.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | Unique per form on the page, for example footer-newsletter |
| `source` | `string` | no | Lead source sent with the generate_lead tracking event. Default: the id |
| `label` | `string` | no | Visible label. Default: the translated "Join the list" |
| `text` | `string` | no | Optional supporting sentence under the label |

```liquid
{% render 'newsletter', id: 'footer-newsletter', source: 'footer_newsletter' %}
```

## pagination

File: `snippets/pagination.liquid`

Pagination for a {% paginate %} object. Two styles:

- numbered (default): accessible page links, crawlable, no JavaScript.
- show_more: a "Show more" button that is a REAL link to the next page
  (rel="next"). Crawlers follow it, every ?page=N stays a self-canonical,
  indexable page, and without JavaScript it simply navigates. With JavaScript
  (assets/show-more.js) a normal click loads the next page's products into the
  list in place, announces "Showing N of M", moves focus to the first new
  product, and survives Back through history.state. Modified clicks (new tab)
  follow the link.

Do not add rel="nofollow" to pagination links: it hides deeper pages from
crawlers. Page N titles and self-referencing canonicals come from
snippets/meta-tags.liquid and Shopify.

The list that grows needs the attribute data-show-more-list.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paginate` | `object` | yes | The paginate object from {% paginate %} |
| `type` | `string` | no | numbered (default) or show_more |
| `page_items` | `number` | no | Items on this page (show_more) |
| `total` | `number` | no | Items in the whole result (show_more) |
| `section_id` | `string` | no | section.id of the calling section (show_more) |

```liquid
{% render 'pagination', paginate: paginate, type: 'show_more', page_items: collection.products.size, total: collection.products_count, section_id: section.id %}
```

## payment-icons

File: `snippets/payment-icons.liquid`

The payment methods the store accepts, as a row of small icons: one image per entry of `shop.enabled_payment_types`,
from Shopify's own payment icon set (served from Shopify's CDN, never built by hand), each named for screen readers
with its type ("Visa", "Apple pay"). Renders nothing when the store has none. Used by the footer and by
blocks/payment-icons.liquid. Decision record: docs/decisions/034-payment-icons-are-one-snippet-with-a-one-color-option.md.

The one color option turns the icons to grayscale and softens them (CSS only). The icons are not recolored to a
single brand color: Shopify's images are full color cards, so grayscale is the honest "monochrome".

| `mono` | `boolean` | no | Show the icons in grayscale |
| `class` | `string` | no | Extra class on the list |

```liquid
{% render 'payment-icons', mono: true %}
```

## placeholder-pick

File: `snippets/placeholder-pick.liquid`

Picks the placeholder image entry for a product that has no image: prints the handle of the best matching entry of
the metaobject type product_placeholder, or nothing when no entry matches. The caller reads that entry's image with
`shop.metaobjects.product_placeholder[handle].image.value` (see snippets/product-card.liquid; a list cannot be indexed
by position in Liquid, a lookup by handle works) and falls back to the theme setting "Product placeholder image". Decision record: docs/decisions/038-placeholder-images-by-type-and-vendor.md.

An entry has an optional product type and an optional vendor (empty means any). It matches when each field it
sets equals the product's (ignoring case). The most specific match wins: type and vendor, then type only, then
vendor only; the first entry wins a tie. An entry that sets neither is never picked (the theme setting is the
default). At most 24 entries are read. A leaf snippet on purpose: it renders nothing, so no render is nested
deeper than the card's own image (AGENTS.md rule 7).

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product` | `product` | yes | The product with no image |

```liquid
{%- capture pick -%}{%- render 'placeholder-pick', product: product -%}{%- endcapture -%}
```

## placeholder

File: `snippets/placeholder.liquid`

Editor-only hint for unfinished content. Renders a dashed box only while the
store is being edited or previewed: the theme editor, the editor's visual
preview, or an unpublished or development theme. In production it renders
nothing, so unfinished content can never ship to customers.

Fail-closed: if the signals are missing or change, the hint stays hidden.
`theme.role` is deprecated by Shopify, so it is only ever used to ADD preview
contexts, never to decide that something is safe to show.

The label is editor-facing English and intentionally not translated: it
never reaches a customer.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | yes | What the merchant should do here |
| `wide` | `boolean` | no | Use the tall variant for section-sized gaps |

```liquid
{% render 'placeholder', label: 'Hero: choose an image and add blocks', wide: true %}
```

## product-card

File: `snippets/product-card.liquid`

Product card. Renders its own <li>, so call it inside a <ul role="list"> and do
not wrap it. Minimal markup on purpose: this runs once per product, so every
node here is multiplied by the page size. The li is the card, the image is a
direct child (no media wrapper), the title link stretches over the card with
::after, and the badge is positioned against the li.

A product with no image shows the placeholder chosen by its type and vendor (the metaobject product_placeholder,
decision 038), else settings.placeholder_image when the merchant set one,
otherwise an empty neutral block of the same shape, so the grid never shifts.

Why one stretched link and not a wrapper link: docs/decisions/001-stretched-card-link.md.

Only image and price are rendered inside; do not nest further snippets here.
The wishlist heart is one button, drawn with a CSS mask (no SVG), shown when the
Wishlist theme settings allow it. Its behavior lives in assets/wishlist.js.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product` | `product` | yes | The product to render |
| `eager` | `boolean` | no | Load the image eagerly (first row only) |
| `sizes` | `string` | no | Image sizes attribute |
| `heading` | `string` | no | Heading element for the title: h2 under a page h1, h3 under an h2 section. Default: h3 |

```liquid
<ul class="product-grid" role="list">
  {% render 'product-card', product: product, eager: true, heading: 'h2' %}
</ul>
```

File: `snippets/product-grid.liquid`

A grid of product cards from one collection, plus the list-view tracking event when tracking
is on. Shared by sections/featured-collection.liquid and blocks/product-grid.liquid so a grid
looks and measures the same wherever it appears.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## product-zoom

File: `snippets/product-zoom.liquid`

The full screen image viewer of the product page: one native <dialog>, opened by the zoom buttons that
sections/main-product.liquid puts over each gallery image. assets/zoom.js fills it. Decision record:
docs/decisions/014-product-image-zoom-is-a-native-dialog.md.

The viewer is a column of screens, one image per screen with no padding: the whole image, a line of caption
under it (the description without any "AI generated" wording and, when the image belongs to variants, "Shown for:
Moss / M"), the image count "1 / 2" in the top start corner when there are several images, and nothing pushed
out of the viewport, however long the caption. Scrolling snaps from image to image (wheel, finger or scroll bar; pinch zoom works natively);
the arrow keys and Space jump too. The image the shopper pressed is in view when it opens, and Escape or the
close button return to the gallery with focus on the button that opened it.

The images are built by the script the first time the viewer opens, so a page nobody zooms carries only this
shell. The image width and height attributes of the one <img> in the markup are only there for the markup rules.

Focus starts on the scrolling area (autofocus), not on a button: Space on a focused Close button would close
the viewer instead of moving to the next image. The dialog is modal, so the page behind it is inert.

Rendered once per page, only when the setting "Let shoppers zoom product images" is on.

```liquid
{% render 'product-zoom' %}
```

## quantity-input

File: `snippets/quantity-input.liquid`

Quantity stepper: minus button, number input, plus button. Without JavaScript
it is a plain number input (the buttons stay invisible but keep their space until assets/quantity-input.js
upgrades the element). The buttons use aria-disabled at the limits so keyboard
focus is never lost, and a polite live region announces the new value.

Pair it with a <label for="{{ id }}"> (visible or visually hidden). Stepping
fires a normal `change` event, so forms and assets/cart-items.js react as if
the number had been typed.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | id of the input, for the label |
| `name` | `string` | yes | name of the input |
| `value` | `number` | yes | current quantity |
| `min` | `number` | no | lowest allowed quantity (the variant's quantity rule). Default: 1 |
| `max` | `number` | no | highest value: the rule's maximum or the stock, whichever is lower |
| `increment` | `number` | no | the quantity moves in steps of this size from the minimum (a rule). Default: 1 |
| `zero` | `boolean` | no | 0 is also allowed: the cart, where 0 removes the line |
| `hint_max` | `number` | no | the rule's own maximum, named in the hint. Stock is never named (decision 015) |
| `line` | `number` | no | cart line number: adds data-quantity and data-line for cart-items.js A hint under the control names the non-default limits ("Minimum 6 · Multiples of 6 · Maximum 24") and is the input's description. With no rule there is no hint. Decision record: docs/decisions/015-quantity-limits-follow-the-rule-and-never-name-the-stock.md. |

```liquid
{% render 'quantity-input', id: 'quantity-main', name: 'quantity', value: 1 %}
```

## schema-site

File: `snippets/schema-site.liquid`

Organization and WebSite structured data for the home page, as one linked

@graph. The @id values are reused by other schema snippets so the pieces
connect: `/#organization` and `/#website`.

- Organization: name, url, logo (ImageObject), sameAs from the Social profile URLs theme setting. Extend with contactPoint, address or
hasMerchantReturnPolicy for a specific brand here, not elsewhere. - WebSite: SearchAction pointing at the store search.

Render only on the home page. Every string goes through `json`.

```liquid
{% render 'schema-site' %}
```

## search-results

File: `snippets/search-results.liquid`

The results under the header search field (one ARIA listbox) and their styles. Rendered by
sections/predictive-search.liquid for each request, and rendered once, empty, by the header so
these styles are on every page: the section is only ever fetched, never placed, so a
stylesheet of its own would never reach the page.

Two parts:
1. Suggestions (the search terms Shopify proposes, then matching collections) are the lower part
   of the search box: they share one border with the field, like Google's extended input.
2. Below the box: the first three matching products (so the whole list fits a phone screen
   without scrolling), pages and articles, and a "Show all for ..." button that goes to the
   full results page.

The links are the options (role="option"); the input is the combobox and points at the active
one with aria-activedescendant while focus stays in the field. They are also normal tab stops: Tab goes from
the field to the suggestions, then the products, pages and the button. data-status carries the sentence announced in a live region.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | `object` | no | The predictive_search object (only available in the section, so it is passed in) |

```liquid
{% render 'search-results', results: predictive_search %}
```

## skeletons

File: `snippets/skeletons.liquid`

Skeleton placeholders for soft navigation. Inert <template> elements that
assets/soft-nav.js clones into <main> while the next page loads. Only
rendered when soft navigation is enabled. Keep the geometry close to the
real page so the swap does not shift layout.

```liquid
{% render 'skeletons' %}
```

## social-links

File: `snippets/social-links.liquid`

The footer's social links: one plain text link per line of the theme setting "Social profile URLs" (the same list
that is published as schema.org sameAs, so there is one source). The link text is the network's name, taken from
the address (Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky, Snapchat, Vimeo);
any other address shows its host name. Text, not logos: no brand artwork to ship, nothing to translate, and
the words are what a screen reader reads. At most twelve links; a line that is not a full address is skipped.
Renders nothing while the setting is empty. Decision record: docs/decisions/028-social-links-are-text-links-from-the-profile-list.md.

```liquid
{% render 'social-links' %}
```

## sticky-buy

File: `snippets/sticky-buy.liquid`

The sticky add to cart bar of the product page: the product title, the chosen options, the price and an
Add to cart button, fixed to the bottom edge of the screen once the buy box has scrolled out of view above and
hidden again when the footer is reached. It is outside the page flow, so nothing moves when it appears.
Decision record: docs/decisions/021-sticky-add-to-cart-submits-the-product-form.md.

The button is not a second form: it submits the product form by its `form` attribute, so the quantity that is
chosen, the add request, the cart drawer, the tracking event and the error message are the ones of the buy box.
The inside of the bar is a `data-swap` region, so assets/product-form.js replaces it from the server's response
when the variant changes (price, options, sold out). Without JavaScript the bar is never shown.

Rendered by blocks/_buy-buttons.liquid when "Show a sticky add to cart bar" is on.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `variant` | yes | the selected or first available variant |
| `form_id` | `string` | yes | id of the product form the button submits |

```liquid
{% render 'sticky-buy', variant: variant, form_id: form_id %}
```

## swatch-background

File: `snippets/swatch-background.liquid`

CSS background for a multi-color swatch: two colors split in halves, three in thirds, on a
45 degree diagonal (top start to bottom end). Outputs nothing for fewer than two colors; a
single color is used as it is by the caller. Plain text with no stray whitespace, so it can be
captured into a style attribute. Used by blocks/_color-siblings.liquid.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `colors` | `object` | yes | A list of hex colors (a list.color metafield value); only the first three count |

```liquid
{% render 'swatch-background', colors: product.metafields.singi.color.value %}
```

## theme-init

File: `snippets/theme-init.liquid`

The theme's one inline script, rendered in the head of both layouts
(`npm run check:rules` allows no other). It does two small things that must
happen before first paint, plus one tiny handler that is not about paint:

1. Color mode. Sets it before paint (no flash) and handles the light/dark toggle.
   A saved choice in localStorage wins over the device setting and the theme's
   default color mode. The toggle button is any element with data-theme-toggle.

2. Product image placeholder. Clicking a link to a product remembers the card
   image the browser has already loaded (its exact URL, so it is in the HTTP
   cache). On the product page that URL is exposed as --placeholder, and the
   first gallery image sits on it (see sections/main-product.liquid) until the
   full-size image arrives, so the hero never flashes empty. It is only used when
   the saved path matches the page and is under 30 seconds old. window.singiPlaceholder()
   re-applies it after a soft navigation.

3. Grid or list view. A saved "list" choice (localStorage singi-view) is put on <html> as
   data-view before first paint, so a collection or search page never shows the grid and then
   jumps to the list. The radios of snippets/view-toggle.liquid follow it after load and after
   a soft navigation, and a change saves the new choice. Decision 010.

4. Dismissed notices. The ids of the notices this visitor dismissed (localStorage singi-dismissed,
   space separated) go on <html> as data-dismissed before first paint, so a section can hide itself
   with one CSS rule and never flash. The announcement bar uses it (decision 027).

5. Search focus. When the header's search panel (a popover) opens, focus moves to its
   input. The HTML autofocus attribute is not used: it would fire on page load instead.
   (assets/predictive-search.js also focuses it inside the tap, which iOS needs for the
   keyboard; this handler covers the moment before that module has loaded.)

```liquid
{% render 'theme-init' %}
```

File: `snippets/tokens.liquid`

Design tokens. Emits

@font-face rules and CSS custom properties from theme

view_cart payload as inert JSON. Rendered inside <cart-items> so it is

in layout/theme.liquid, only when settings.tracking_enabled is on.

## tracking-item

File: `snippets/tracking-item.liquid`

One GA4 item as a JSON object, for a product and a specific variant. Used
on the product page for view_item and for the add-to-cart payload. Not for
loops: lists use the tracking-list snippet.

item_id is the product ID everywhere (lists, product page, cart, pixel) so
GA4 funnels line up. variant_id and sku travel as custom item parameters.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product` | `product` | yes | The product |
| `variant` | `variant` | no | The variant. Default: selected or first available |
| `quantity` | `number` | no | Quantity. Default: 1 |

```liquid

```

## tracking-list

File: `snippets/tracking-list.liquid`

view_item_list payload for a product grid, as inert JSON that
assets/tracking.js forwards. One loop, no nested renders. Render it next to
the grid it describes, inside <main>, so soft navigation and filtering pick
up the new list.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `products` | `object` | yes | Array of products (a collection page slice, or search results) |
| `list_id` | `string` | yes | GA4 item_list_id |
| `list_name` | `string` | yes | GA4 item_list_name |
| `limit` | `number` | no | Maximum items. Default: 50 |
| `offset` | `number` | no | Items before this page, for the GA4 index. Default: 0 |
| `only_products` | `boolean` | no | Skip non-product results (search) |

```liquid
{% render 'tracking-list', products: collection.products, list_id: collection.handle, list_name: collection.title, offset: paginate.current_offset %}
```

## unit-price

File: `snippets/unit-price.liquid`

Unit price of a variant, for comparing sizes: "$78.00 / 100 ml". Renders nothing when the
variant has no unit price set. Shopify's own filter (unit_price_with_measurement) prints
"$78.00/100ml" and cannot be spaced, so the pieces are formatted here: the price with the
store's money format, a reference value of 1 left out ("$24.00 / L", not "/ 1 L"), and unit
symbols written the usual way (L, m², ft²). Shopify returns the unit lowercase.

Screen readers get a full sentence instead of the slash (products.unit_price_per, for example
"$78.00 per 100 ml"), so each language keeps its own word order.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `variant` | yes | The variant |
| `part` | `string` | no | 'visible' for the text shown, 'label' for the screen reader sentence. Both are plain text with ordinary spaces (assets/product-form.js reads them from data attributes). Default: the finished <p> with both. |

```liquid
{% render 'unit-price', variant: product.selected_or_first_available_variant %}
```

## view-toggle

File: `snippets/view-toggle.liquid`

Grid or list view for a page of product cards, with no JavaScript: two radio chips (the same
.chip pattern as the variant picker) and a few CSS rules that react to the checked one with
:has() on the wrapper. Render it inside <div class="view-wrap">, BEFORE <facets-form>: facets.js
replaces everything inside facets-form on every filter change, so a toggle inside it would reset to
the grid each time.

The choice is remembered: snippets/theme-init.liquid saves it (localStorage singi-view), puts a saved
"list" on <html> as data-view before first paint (so there is no flash of the grid) and keeps these radios
in step. Without JavaScript the radios still work, but nothing is remembered and the grid is the default.
Decision record: docs/decisions/010-grid-and-list-view-without-javascript.md.

The toggle sits on the filter bar's line, at its end: the bar leaves room for it (padding-inline-end on
.facets) and the toggle is placed over that room. All of it is logical properties, so it mirrors in right to left.

In the list view the card's image is a fixed 7.5rem column and the text sits beside it. The card's
absolutely placed parts (AI label, favorite heart) are positioned against the image's corner, not the card's. The sold out badge moves into the text column, above the title, because the narrow image has no room for it beside the heart. The quick add button (when on) keeps the image's bottom start corner, and a card's video preview (when on) is as wide as the image. The text is centered beside the image with two spacer rows.

```liquid
<div class="view-wrap">
  {% render 'view-toggle' %}
  <facets-form>...</facets-form>
</div>
```

## wishlist-item

File: `snippets/wishlist-item.liquid`

One saved product as a cart-style row: thumbnail, title, price and two small icon
controls. The first is exactly one of three states: a primary add to cart (the saved
variant, or the only variant, is available: adds it at once), the same button disabled
with a check once that variant is in the cart (assets/wishlist.js switches it as the cart
changes), or a secondary link with an arrow to the product page (a variant has to be
chosen, or it is sold out). The second is the pressed heart (the same secondary button as
on the product page; it removes the item). Fetched by assets/wishlist.js through
templates/product.wishlist.liquid.

Self-contained on purpose: it owns its CSS. The cart page renders this snippet
once without a product (it outputs nothing) so Shopify includes the CSS there,
because the rows themselves are inserted by JavaScript.

The saved variant arrives as ?variant=ID (product.selected_variant), so the row shows
that variant's title, price, image and stock.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product` | `product` | no | The saved product. Without one the snippet only carries its CSS. |

```liquid
{% render 'wishlist-item', product: product %}
```
